# Managing chronic conditions

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Basics of internal medicine > Managing chronic conditions*

[Original Article Link](/library/gs0F8h)

---

## Summary

Chronic conditions and diseases affect over 50% of adults. They are associated with ongoing medical care and/or impaired <u>activities of daily living</u> as well as increased <u>morbidity</u>, mortality, and health care costs. Studies have shown that patients have improved health outcomes if they are knowledgeable about their chronic condition as well as engaged and confident in managing the condition. Clinicians should provide tailored patient education and use <u>shared decision-making</u> when caring for patients with or at risk for chronic conditions. For patients who are struggling to adhere to recommended treatment, exploring and addressing specific patient-related and systemic barriers may increase engagement.




See also “<u>Patient communication and counseling</u>,” “<u>Patient-centered approach</u>,” “<u>Motivational interviewing</u>,” and “<u>Preventive medicine</u>.”

---

## Treatment adherence

### Overview




* Definition: the extent to which an individual follows recommendations from a <u>health care professional</u>.

* Five dimensions of adherence (according to the WHO) [[21]](/library/kCbmHD)

* Social and economic factors (e.g., social support, cultural context, access to transportation)

* Health care team and system-related factors (e.g., time constraints, communication skills of provider, cost of care)

* Therapy-related factors (e.g., complexity of treatment plans, adverse effects, dosage frequency)

* Patient-related factors (e.g., <u>self-efficacy</u>, motivation, <u>health literacy</u>)

* Condition-related factors (e.g., symptom burden, prognosis, comorbidities)





> [!TIP]
> Physicians should identify potential barriers to <u>treatment adherence</u> and implement strategies to encourage adherence using a <u>patient-centered approach</u>.




### <u>Risk factors for poor adherence</u>




#### Patient-related factors and interventions




| <br>Patient-related factors affecting adherence [[22]](/library/dGcoyd0)[[23]](/library/VwYG3r)<br> |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Factors |  | Recommendations |
| <br>Limited comprehension <br> |  | <br><br>* Provide ≤ 3 takeaway points per visit; repeat and reinforce them.  [[24]](/library/HscKwd0)<br><br>* Provide written and verbal instructions that are at a 5<sup>th</sup>– 6<sup>th</sup> grade reading level. [[25]](/library/VGcGyd0)<br><br>* Utilize the <u>teach-back method</u>. [[6]](/library/GFcBjV0)[[26]](/library/jJc_FW0)<br><br>* Ask what helps the patient best learn and remember things.<br><br>* Assess for and accommodate any <u>hearing</u> and/or visual impairments.<br><br><br> |
| <br><u>Health illiteracy</u><br>(including technological literacy) |  | <br><br>* Consider referral to a chronic disease self-management program (see “Tips and links”). [[27]](/library/8scO9d0)<br><br>* Provide in-person instruction and/or online videos demonstrating how to navigate <u>health systems</u> (e.g., how to use patient portals).<br><br>* Provide digital and/or printed patient health passports.  [[28]](/library/CscqCd0)<br><br><br> |
| Forgetfulness |  | <br><br>* For patients who unintentionally miss medication doses, consider the following:<br><br>* <u>Blister</u> packs or weekly pillboxes<br><br>* Alarms or app-based medication reminders  [[29]](/library/ZscZtd0)<br><br>* Electronic pill monitoring<br><br>* Consider <u>dementia screening</u> (e.g., <u>MMSE</u>) in older patients.<br><br><br> |
| Lack of motivation |  | <br><br>* Recognize and encourage when patient actions directly lead to improved symptoms and/or diagnostic results.<br><br>* Ask the patient to suggest solutions.<br><br>* Remind the patient of the benefits of healthier habits.<br><br>* Refer for <u>motivational interviewing</u>.<br><br>* <u>Screen for depression</u> (e.g., <u>PHQ-9</u>) and refer if indicated.<br><br>* Ensure a follow-up visit is scheduled before the patient leaves.<br><br><br> |
| <br>Limited accessibility <br> |  | <br><br>* Consider using <u>telehealth</u> visits for follow-up encounters.<br><br>* Utilize patient portals and/or telephone calls for patient updates.<br><br>* Book tests at the end of the last visit.<br><br><br> |
| Cultural differences |  | <br><br>* Use qualified medical interpreters when needed.   [[30]](/library/uFcpPV0)<br><br>* If necessary, acknowledge cultural differences (see also “<u>Culture in the health care setting</u>”).<br><br><br> |
| <br>Lack of support, stigmatization<br>(especially among <u>adolescents</u>, e.g., due to peer attitudes toward the illness and/or its treatment) [[31]](/library/QJcuFW0)<br> |  | <br><br>* If patients give permission to have a support person present, include them in the conversations.<br><br>* Peer-facilitated behavioral interventions to convey knowledge about the illness and social acceptance for its treatment [[32]](/library/PJcW8W0)[[33]](/library/4Jc38W0)<br><br>* Encourage patients with chronic illnesses to seek support from peers with the same chronic illness, e.g., through:<br><br>* Community health projects<br><br>* Local and online support groups<br><br>* Encourage patients with chronic illnesses to familiarize their peers with their illness and its treatment.<br><br><br> |





> [!TIP]
> A patient's recall rate decreases when ≥ 3 pieces of information are given in one visit; summarize information and ask the patient to repeat back the management plan. [[34]](/library/xscECd0)




#### Care-related factors and interventions [[22]](/library/dGcoyd0)




| <br>Care-related factors affecting adherence [[22]](/library/dGcoyd0)<br> |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Factors |  | Recommendations |  |
| <br>Medical costs  [[35]](/library/EFc8PV0)<br> |  | <br><br>* Medications<br><br>* <u>Review medications</u> and stop any unnecessary prescriptions.<br><br>* Order insurance companies' preferred drugs.<br><br>* Offer 90-day supplies rather than 30-day supplies when possible.<br><br>* Suggest discounted cash-pay medications.<br><br>* Consider utilizing technology for patient follow-ups (e.g., portal, telephone, <u>telehealth</u> visits) rather than more expensive in-office visits.<br><br>* Consider consultation with a social worker.<br><br><br> |  |
| <u>Polypharmacy</u>,<br>complex and/or<br>inconvenient treatment plans |  | <br><br>* Simplify whenever possible.<br><br>* Stop unnecessary medications.<br><br>* Consider combination tablets to reduce the pill burden.<br><br>* Use less frequent dosing.  [[36]](/library/WscPFd0)<br><br>* Group specialist appointments on the same day, if possible.<br><br><br> |  |
| Adverse effects of medication |  | <br><br>* Discuss medication side effects.<br><br>* Lower doses and/or split dosing.  [[36]](/library/WscPFd0)<br><br>* Ensure appropriate administration times.  [[37]](/library/1sc2Fd0)<br><br>* Avoid coadministration with medications that might potentiate side effects. [[38]](/library/cscaFd0)<br><br>* In patients with severe or persistent side effects, swap to an alternative medication if possible.<br><br><br> |  |
| Clinical time constraints |  | <br>* Maximize time with the patient. [[39]](/library/Fscg9d0)<br><br> | <br><br>* Before the appointment, ensure required diagnostic studies have been performed.<br><br>* On the day of the appointment:<br><br>* Use morning huddles to prepare.<br><br>* Provide follow-up forms at check-in.<br><br>* Pick a few things to address during the visit.<br><br><br> |
| <br>* Automate tasks.<br><br> | <br><br>* Develop individualized <u>care plans</u>.<br><br>* Customize encounter templates.<br><br>* Update the problem list.<br><br>* Send automated reminders: Use patient portals, email reminder programs, and/or telephone calls to:<br><br>* Send reminders about appointments<br><br>* Reinforce education<br><br>* Highlight treatment goals<br><br><br> |  |  |





> [!TIP]
> Factors affecting <u>treatment adherence</u> are dynamic, complex, and manifold; engage empathetically with the patient and avoid blame or judgment.
